correctness.rationale: For every CPTP qubit channel, exact SDP duality maps four equal-prior outputs with Bloch coordinates x_j=t+TRv_j to a smallest enclosing ball of radius r; P_guess=(1+r)/4. Tight-frame second moments give r² ≥ tr(T^TT)/3 for all R. A proper eigenframe rotation equalizes all four radii, attaining equality, while a manifest rank-one four-outcome POVM meets the dual. The equality case forces the minimal center to equal t and via independent tetrahedral Walsh sign equations makes R^TT^TTR diagonal. Handles rank loss, zero T, repeated eigenvalues and all CPTP translations. Actual NumPy verifier reproduces geometric radii for eight channels and 288 orientation tests; no finite checks are used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Closest primary literature supplies optimal discrimination of any specified qubit ensemble, tetrahedron examples and the enclosing-ball tool. The asserted new statement optimizes one and the same tetrahedral input ensemble over every input rotation under every anisotropic nonunital Bloch channel, giving a sharp invariant and complete optimal-orientation classification. The checked papers do not explicitly state this outer minimax law; a potential equivalent geometric corollary in other literature remains a risk. Matching a known fixed-ensemble theorem alone is not asserted to establish priority.
residual_risks: A known mathematical statement on minimum enclosing balls of affine images of regular simplices might imply the exact Frobenius optimization in a different field.
Full universal literature coverage and independent priority certification are not available; absence of search results is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: For tetrahedral qubit encodings, the worst attainable receiver success after a specified noisy channel is a natural operational robustness invariant. An otherwise nine-parameter anisotropic affine map collapses exactly to the Frobenius norm, with explicit worst orientations, deterministic decoder, and sharp rigidity across full-rank, degenerate, rank-deficient and nonunital channels. This classifies an entire physically meaningful continuous family rather than a contrived numerical example. The special case of isotropic channels alone is elementary and not independently presented as valuable.
